clue.text: Complimentary bar's last to open

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word is taken away from the end and made to stand at the start instead

blocks.note: a reef is a bar of rock or sand just below the sea

explanation.surface: A pub announces that its last drink before opening time is on the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar is a sandbar, REEF; its last letter F moves to the front to give FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complimentary is given without charge, as with a complimentary ticket handed out by a theatre.

clue.text: Exploit dictator's measures

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone who dictates, speaking words for another to write down, so we go by sound

blocks.note: feet are units of length, measures

explanation.surface: A tyrant's policies are exploited by others.
explanation.walkthrough: Dictator suggests a tyrant, but it means one who dictates aloud, so FEET is spoken and heard as FEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit, as a noun, is a daring deed or notable achievement, which is exactly what a feat is.

clue.text: Noble award provides location for stud?

blocks.note: an earl is a nobleman
Order of the British Empire, an honour conferred in Britain

explanation.surface: A peer's honour is pinned on as if it were a stud on his lapel.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour (Officer of the Order of the British Empire). The question mark flags a definition by example: a stud earring goes there.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud earring is worn through the soft lower lobe of the ear, so that lobe is a place to put one.

clue.text: Insubstantial part of growth industry

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, a run of letters straddling them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A booming sector is dismissed as flimsy in one of its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin can describe an argument or excuse that lacks substance and is weak or unconvincing.

clue.text: Murdered soldier finally found beside tracks popular with public

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of each of the two words that follow it

blocks.note: a hit is a contract killing, so to be hit is to be murdered
a para is a paratrooper
the final letter of found
the final letter of beside

explanation.surface: A soldier is found dead next to railway lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tracks' looks like railway lines beside which a body lies; here it means recorded songs, and 'finally' takes the last letter of both found and beside.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade is the chart of best-selling records, the songs most popular with buyers at a given time.

clue.text: Scrub opening of wound in need of dressing

indicators.note: to scrub is to cancel, so the first letter of the next word is cancelled

blocks.note: wound as the past tense of wind: twisted along a path

explanation.surface: A nurse cleans the edge of an injury that still needs bandaging.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound reads as an injury and dressing as a bandage; in fact wound rhymes with sound and means SNAKED, and dressing is putting clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone naked has no clothes on and so needs to get dressed before going out.

clue.text: Good family introduces leading man

indicators.note: the second item comes first and leads into the first, so the order is swapped

blocks.note: kin are one's relatives
G is a standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A wholesome family presents the star of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is the man at the head of a nation, the one who leads its people.

clue.text: Class muddled three Rs with teenage instructor

indicators.note: something muddled is jumbled up, so the letters that follow are mixed

blocks.note: a class is a kind or sort
three letters R
taken as written

explanation.surface: A class gets the three Rs confused with the help of an adolescent teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, sound like a lesson, but are just three letter Rs to shuffle with teenage.
explanation.definitionFit: A kindergartener can mean a teacher in a kindergarten, the nursery class for the youngest children.

clue.text: Most unsophisticated Scotsman lifted top

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word turns it upwards so it is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Ian is the standard crossword Scottish first name
a vest is a top worn on the upper body

explanation.surface: The most gullible Scot has his shirt stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: Lifted suggests stealing; in a down answer it turns IAN upward into NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and inexperienced, so the naivest person is the least worldly of all.

clue.text: Picture with controversial contents changed by The Sun?

blocks.note: a photograph is a picture
sensitive material is touchy, controversial matter

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper doctors a scandalous picture before printing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun looks like the British tabloid newspaper, which would be expected to alter a racy photo, but it is the star whose light alters the substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A photosensitive material reacts chemically when exposed to light, as sunlight does to photographic film or certain skin.

clue.text: I didn't hear that engineer's announcement

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the name is to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame

explanation.surface: Someone at a public address misses what the engineer has just said.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-word question is how people ask a speaker to repeat something they failed to catch.

clue.text: Express blasted failure to strike?

blocks.note: to air a view is to express it
blasted as in fired, shot

explanation.surface: A train or newspaper called the Express has been damaged by a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: Express could be a train or a newspaper; it is the verb to voice an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket an air shot is a swing that misses the ball entirely, a whiff.

clue.text: Revolutionary thinkers suppressing resistance from home counties

indicators.note: a revolution overturns everything, so the letters of the next word are thrown into a new order
to suppress something is to stifle it so it does not appear, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Radical philosophers silence opposition in the area around London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is one of the home counties, those surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentish describes people or things belonging to Kent, a county in the ring around London.

clue.text: What could turn Hard Left, keen to adopt terms of Corbyn and lunatic fringe

indicators.note: a term is an end point, so only the final letter of each of the following words counts
to adopt is to take in, so some letters are placed inside the word before

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
to keen is to wail in mourning
the final letter of Corbyn
the final letter of and
the final letter of lunatic
the final letter of fringe

explanation.surface: A political tirade about the hard left, Jeremy Corbyn and the lunatic fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: Corbyn was the left-wing Labour leader, so the surface reads as politics; Hard is the definition's state, not hard-line. Last letters of four words go inside LAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Portland cement is the common building cement which sets solid when mixed with water, so it is what could become hard.

clue.text: Bishop follows this female sage?

indicators.note: the clergyman follows the word after it, so he goes at the end

blocks.note: the female pronoun
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is a follower of a wise woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage reads as a wise person to follow; the question mark warns that it is an example of a plant used in cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is a culinary plant whose leaves flavour food, one example of a herb.

clue.text: Odds? Yes and no

blocks.note: first meaning: betting odds of one to one
second meaning: an equal chance either way, as likely to be one as the other

explanation.walkthrough: Odds and evens look like opposites, yet here one is the definition of the other: the betting price where a win doubles the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens are betting odds of one to one, given when an outcome is as likely as not, a fifty-fifty chance.

clue.text: Presumptuously claims spa town's demolishing hotel

indicators.note: demolishing knocks something down so it is gone, here a letter is removed

blocks.note: Harrogate is a spa town in Yorkshire; with the 's
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire spa town knocks down one of its hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to seize or lay claim to something without having any right to it.

clue.text: Absorbent canvas opens up on middle of river

indicators.note: the central letters of the next word are kept and its ends dropped
in a down entry, the word that opens is placed up at the top before the rest

blocks.note: re means on, concerning
a tent is made of canvas
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sponge-like canvas is unrolled beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, a Latin-derived word for on or about, goes at the top, then TENT and the middle of river.
explanation.definitionFit: Retentive describes a material that holds on to water or other things, soaking them up and keeping them.

clue.text: Models chastised about clothes

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the word wraps around the answer inside it
about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read the other way

blocks.note: four letters inside this word

explanation.surface: Fashion models are scolded about what they are wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes looks like a noun for garments; it is a verb, the word hiding the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To model for an artist is to sit, posing still while being painted or photographed.

clue.text: Most powerful elite guards in conflict retreated

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the word for elite surrounds the rest
retreating means going backwards, so these letters are read the other way

blocks.note: the elite are the best
taken as written
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Elite troops pull back during a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawny means muscular and physically strong, so the brawniest is the strongest of all.

clue.text: Incontinent men receiving treatment for inability to retain things

indicators.note: treatment works on something and changes it, so the letters are rearranged
receiving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: split as in continent: Asia is a continent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Incontinent men are given medical treatment for a problem with retention.
explanation.walkthrough: Incontinent suggests a medical condition and retain sounds like bladder control; it breaks into in continent, ASIA. Retaining things here is memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the inability to keep facts and experiences in mind.

clue.text: Joint work schedules must have end of shift moved

indicators.note: end asks for the closing letter of the next word
a letter moved is taken out of its place and set down elsewhere, here at the back

blocks.note: rotas are timetables of who works when
the final letter of shift

explanation.surface: Shared work rosters have to change when a shift finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The T in ROTAS is the last letter of shift; moving it to the end turns ROTAS into ROAST. Joint looks like shared but is a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a large cut of meat cooked in the oven, the Sunday joint.

clue.text: Adult cannot welcome what may be seen around ancient capital

definitions.text: what may be seen around ancient capital

blocks.note: A is the film classification for adult
can't, cannot shortened
hi is a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A grown-up is unable to greet visitors near an old seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital suggests a city; it is the carved top of a column, which in Corinthian style is ringed with leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthi are the stylised acanthus leaves carved round the tops of classical Corinthian columns.

clue.text: Preliminary survey by staff overlooking Conservative polymath

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so the abbreviation is dropped

blocks.note: a reconnaissance surveys ground before action
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A first survey by employees ignores the Tory party, according to a learned expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A Renaissance man has wide learning and talent across many fields, like Leonardo da Vinci.

clue.text: Water is extracted from fruit

indicators.note: extracted means pulled out, so these letters come out of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
a raisin is a dried grape

explanation.surface: Juice is squeezed out of a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain is water falling from clouds in drops, so water serves as its general term.

clue.text: Simultaneous discharge from colossal volcanoes

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of the following words, which contain them

blocks.note: the end of the first word with the start of the second

explanation.surface: Giant volcanoes erupt all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is the firing of several guns together, one simultaneous burst of fire.

clue.text: Cite article about chronic fatigue syndrome

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the article is read backwards

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis

explanation.surface: A writer quotes a paper on a long-term exhaustion illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite something is to mention or refer to it by name, as in citing an example.

clue.text: Implant isn't involved in harmful case

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are jumbled
in sends the jumbled letters inside another word
a case surrounds its contents, so the word before it is the outer casing

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
ill as in harmful, ill effects

explanation.surface: A medical implant is not to blame in a damaging lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Case looks like a legal action; it tells us ILL is the casing for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to implant it gradually in someone's mind; the US spelling has the double L.

clue.text: Reason for not moving home affected irate neighbours

indicators.note: something affected is changed, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
neighbours sit side by side, so the two pieces simply go next to each other

blocks.note: at home is in
taken as written

explanation.surface: Angry neighbours are the reason a family won't move house.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving home reads like relocating; home is IN, and moving is physical motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency of a body to stay at rest, or a person's reluctance to act or change.

clue.text: Tolerate appropriate point of view

blocks.note: first meaning: put up with
second meaning: seize for oneself
third meaning: one's opinion on something

explanation.walkthrough: Appropriate looks like an adjective describing the point of view, but it is a verb, and the clue has three separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to bear something, to seize something, and, as a noun, a personal interpretation of an issue.

clue.text: Empty offices filled with unfinished modern units?

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides and keeps only its outer letters
unfinished means the last letter is cut off
filling something places other letters inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of offices
new is modern

explanation.surface: Vacant office blocks are fitted out with half-built modern units.
explanation.walkthrough: Units suggests office or kitchen units; the question mark marks the number sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ones are single units in counting, and the ones column holds the units digit.

clue.text: Married couple seizes opportunity to do something

indicators.note: seizing something means grabbing hold of it, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: to tie is to couple, join
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A newly-wed pair grabs the chance to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: Having time for something means having the chance or occasion to do it.
